featureGroups.label: Rendering
featureGroups.description: Compare where HTML is produced, when it is sent, and how much client runtime is needed.

featureGroups.label: Routing & layouts
featureGroups.description: Compare URL matching, nested composition, navigation, and advanced route behavior.

featureGroups.label: Data & caching
featureGroups.description: Check cache lifetime, request deduplication, invalidation, and whether the mechanism needs a CDN.

featureGroups.label: Server & APIs
featureGroups.description: Compare generated function calls, ordinary HTTP endpoints, form handling, and request middleware.

featureGroups.label: Database
featureGroups.description: Compare data models and query builders, schema migrations, and transactions. Database drivers and external services are identified separately.

featureGroups.label: Backend services
featureGroups.description: Compare durable jobs, email, uploads and real-time delivery. In-process callbacks are not durable job queues.

featureGroups.label: Styling
featureGroups.description: Distinguish built-in compilation from compatible external libraries and app-owned CSS.

featureGroups.label: Images, fonts & scripts
featureGroups.description: Check whether assets are transformed automatically, optimized at build time, or prepared manually.

featureGroups.label: Metadata & SEO
featureGroups.description: Compare structured metadata, inheritance, child overrides, title composition, and generated assets. Select a Metadata API cell for its design assessment.

featureGroups.label: Content
featureGroups.description: Compare Markdown integration, typed content collections, and editorial preview workflows.

featureGroups.label: Internationalization
featureGroups.description: Compare message catalogs, locale-specific URLs, and locale-sensitive formatting separately.

featureGroups.label: Security & auth
featureGroups.description: Check what the framework enforces, what an auth package adds, and what the application must implement.

featureGroups.label: Accessibility
featureGroups.description: Compare navigation focus and announcements separately from tools that check authored markup. No entry certifies that an application is accessible.

featureGroups.label: Developer tooling
featureGroups.description: Compare type checking, dev feedback, project commands, and production bundle inspection.

featureGroups.label: Testing & observability
featureGroups.description: Distinguish framework hooks from external test runners and monitoring services.

featureGroups.label: Deployment
featureGroups.description: Check feature availability on the actual target. Static export and edge runtimes often have restrictions.

features.label: SSR
features.definition: Generate page HTML on the server from application data.

features.label: HTML streaming
features.definition: Send HTML incrementally in the original response. Data streaming and separately fetched fragments are identified in notes.

features.label: Suspense / async UI
features.definition: A declarative boundary with pending UI while asynchronous content resolves. It need not be named Suspense.

features.label: Client activation
features.definition: Make server HTML interactive through hydration, resumability, adoption, or islands. Notes name the mechanism.

features.label: Static generation
features.definition: A workflow that exports deployable HTML before requests arrive. Returning a string alone does not qualify.

features.label: Client rendering
features.definition: Create and update application UI in the browser without requiring initial server HTML.

features.label: Server-only components
features.definition: Keep component implementation and dependencies off the client. Notes distinguish RSC, islands, and server templates.

features.label: Static + dynamic UI
features.definition: Combine a prebuilt shell with request-time content. Notes distinguish original-response streaming from separate island requests.

features.label: URL routing
features.definition: Map application URLs to pages or handlers. A navigation stack alone is distinguished from HTTP routing.

features.label: Nested layouts
features.definition: Compose shared layout UI around nested pages; notes explain whether layout selection is automatic or explicit.

features.label: Route parameters
features.definition: Match variable URL segments, with a documented API for retrieving route parameters.

features.label: Parallel routes
features.definition: Display independently navigable routed regions in one layout. Rendering two ordinary components does not qualify.

features.label: Route interception
features.definition: Render a destination inside the current UI context, such as a routed modal, while preserving direct-link behavior.

features.label: Link prefetching
features.definition: Fetch a likely destination before navigation; notes identify triggers and what is actually fetched.

features.label: SPA-like navigation
features.definition: Navigate between same-site pages without reloading the whole document, updating the URL/history and page content. Includes client routers and Turbo-style HTML swaps. Prefetching or hydration alone does not qualify.

features.label: Page transitions
features.definition: Coordinate visual animations across page navigation through a documented router or View Transitions integration. Navigating without a reload is separate; ordinary component animations alone do not qualify. Browser support and reduced-motion behavior are noted where relevant.

features.label: Redirects & rewrites
features.definition: Documented URL redirection or internal rewriting APIs; notes distinguish which is supported.

features.label: Server data loading
features.definition: Load asynchronous data for server-rendered UI with a documented application pattern.

features.label: Client queries
features.definition: A query API for browser fetch lifecycle, cache state, or server-to-client data handoff; fetch() alone is not a query cache.

features.label: Request deduplication
features.definition: Reuse equivalent reads within one render/request, distinct from caching between requests.

features.label: Cross-request cache
features.definition: Retain data or rendered output across requests. Notes identify storage, lifetime, and deployment dependencies.

features.label: Cache invalidation
features.definition: Explicitly expire or refresh cached data by key, tag, path, or dependencies.

features.label: Page revalidation
features.definition: Refresh previously generated or cached pages after deployment. Notes distinguish origin regeneration from CDN cache headers.

features.label: HTTP endpoints
features.definition: Define application endpoints for JSON, webhooks, or other HTTP responses.

features.label: Server functions
features.definition: Call server-only application functions from browser code through a framework transport; hand-written HTTP endpoints are identified separately.

features.label: Forms & validation
features.definition: A documented form submission and validation workflow. Notes distinguish transport, input validation, and error feedback.

features.label: Request middleware
features.definition: Run application logic around page/API request handling, including request context or response modification.

features.label: Cookies & sessions
features.definition: Read/write request cookies or use a session API; cookie access alone is not session management.

features.label: CSS Modules
features.definition: Build-time local CSS class names imported as a module.

features.label: Scoped styles
features.definition: Component-local styles whose selectors are scoped by a compiler or framework.

features.label: Tailwind integration
features.definition: A documented setup for the external Tailwind CSS compiler; Tailwind is not counted as framework-owned.

features.label: CSS-in-JS
features.definition: A documented CSS-in-JS integration, including server rendering constraints and any required registry.

features.label: Image optimization
features.definition: Automatic resizing, format conversion, or responsive variant generation. Hand-authored srcset is called out separately.

features.label: Font optimization
features.definition: Self-hosting, preload, subsetting, or fallback-metric tooling; notes identify the actual optimizations.

features.label: Script loading
features.definition: Control when third-party scripts load, including deferred or interaction-driven strategies.

features.label: Static asset serving
features.definition: A supported way to publish files with the deployed application, with paths and caching described.

features.label: Metadata API
features.definition: A structured API for titles, descriptions, canonical URLs, and social metadata. Authoring raw head tags is identified separately.

features.label: Data-driven metadata
features.definition: Compute metadata from request parameters or asynchronous data without duplicating the page data pipeline.

features.label: Layout inheritance
features.definition: Inherit metadata defaults through nested layouts. Notes explain field merge or replacement semantics.

features.label: Child overrides
features.definition: A child page/layout can replace or clear inherited metadata. Nested object replacement and inherited arrays must be explained.

features.label: Title composition
features.definition: Apply ancestor title templates while allowing explicit absolute titles or template reset.

features.label: Generated OG images
features.definition: Generate social preview image bytes through a documented integration; setting an og:image URL alone does not qualify.

features.label: Sitemaps
features.definition: Generate XML sitemaps, including any documented splitting, index, or localization support.

features.label: robots.txt
features.definition: A documented file convention or structured generator for crawler directives.

features.label: Markdown / MDX
features.definition: Render authored Markdown content with a supported build/runtime integration; notes distinguish MDX and Markdown output APIs.

features.label: Content collections
features.definition: Load, validate, and query sets of structured content; a database driver alone is not a content collection API.

features.label: Editorial previews
features.definition: Bypass published/cached content for an authenticated editorial preview workflow.

features.label: Translations
features.definition: Locale-specific message lookup, with documented fallback or interpolation.

features.label: Locale routing
features.definition: Locale-specific URLs, detection, or redirects; translation dictionaries alone do not qualify.

features.label: Locale formatting
features.definition: Locale-sensitive date, number, or plural formatting. Fixed-format helpers are identified separately.

features.label: Authentication
features.definition: Documented identity/authentication integration; route guards and cookies alone are not a complete login system.

features.label: Content Security Policy
features.definition: Configure Content Security Policy directives and enforcement. Notes distinguish HTTP headers, meta policies and hash-based policies; nonce coordination is compared separately.

features.label: Nonce-based CSP
features.definition: Coordinate a per-response unpredictable nonce between the Content-Security-Policy and framework-generated scripts/styles, without requiring unsafe-inline. Notes distinguish automatic generation from a supplied nonce and identify streaming, caching and prerendering restrictions. Setting an arbitrary header or allowing a nonce attribute alone does not qualify.

features.label: CSRF defenses
features.definition: Documented protection for unsafe browser requests. Notes specify origin checks, tokens, scope, and gaps.

features.label: Environment & secrets
features.definition: A documented server/client configuration boundary; application secrets must not be exposed to client bundles.

features.label: Type checking
features.definition: Compile-time types for application code or templates. Notes identify toolchain and scope.

features.label: Dev updates
features.definition: A documented live-reload or hot-update workflow. State-preserving HMR is distinguished from full-page reload.

features.label: Project CLI
features.definition: Commands for scaffolding, developing, or building an application.

features.label: Bundle analysis
features.definition: Inspect production browser/server dependency output and its size, distinct from performance benchmarking.

features.label: Unit / component tests
features.definition: A documented unit/component test workflow; notes identify external runners and unsupported component modes.

features.label: Browser tests
features.definition: A documented browser automation integration or workflow; the test runner is identified separately.

features.label: Instrumentation
features.definition: Hooks or integrations for traces, metrics, or production logging; dashboards/exporters may be separate.

features.label: Error boundaries
features.definition: Render a defined fallback/recovery UI for failed page or component work. HTTP status responses alone are distinguished.

features.label: Self-hosting
features.definition: Run the production application on infrastructure you operate, with a documented server runtime or adapter.

features.label: Static hosting
features.definition: Export files deployable without an application server; notes describe features lost in this mode.

features.label: Containers
features.definition: A documented container deployment workflow or image output.

features.label: Edge runtimes
features.definition: A documented edge/worker deployment adapter or runtime, with limitations identified.

features.label: ORM / query builder
features.definition: A documented model or query API above raw SQL or a database driver.

features.label: Schema migrations
features.definition: Versioned database schema changes with an execution and history mechanism.

features.label: Transactions
features.definition: A documented API for atomic database operations, including commit and rollback.

features.label: Background jobs
features.definition: A persistent queue with workers and job lifecycle handling. In-process tasks are qualified separately.

features.label: Email
features.definition: An integrated mail delivery API; templates, transports and queue support are distinguished in notes.

features.label: File uploads & storage
features.definition: Parse uploaded files and manage storage. Request parsing alone is qualified separately.

features.label: Real-time delivery
features.definition: A documented WebSocket, channel, broadcasting or server-sent event API. Notes distinguish transport from a complete pub/sub service.

features.label: Output escaping
features.definition: An owned HTML output-encoding policy for dynamic values. State default/opt-in behavior, protected contexts, URL handling and raw-output bypasses. Escaping text does not establish safe JavaScript/CSS interpolation or HTML sanitization.

features.label: HTML sanitization
features.definition: A maintained allowlist-based API/integration for accepting untrusted rich HTML while removing dangerous markup. Escaping to text, trusting a raw-HTML wrapper or validating a string is not sanitization.

features.label: Authorization policies
features.definition: A documented permission/policy API for deciding whether a principal may perform an operation on a resource. Authentication, hiding a button or a generic middleware hook alone does not qualify.

features.label: Rate limiting
features.definition: A documented limiter for requests/actions with keys, time windows and rejection behavior. State storage, single-process versus distributed enforcement, and any separately installed package. Arbitrary middleware capability alone does not qualify.

features.label: Progressive forms
features.definition: Documented form submission that reaches the server and produces useful results before JavaScript loads or when it is disabled, with optional client enhancement. SSR HTML alone and browser-only submit handlers do not qualify.

features.label: Optimistic updates
features.definition: A documented mutation workflow that displays an unconfirmed result immediately and reconciles it with success/failure. Pending flags alone do not qualify. State automatic versus application-owned rollback and concurrency limitations.

features.label: Stale request handling
features.definition: A documented data/router mechanism that suppresses stale results or cancels superseded requests. Identify which behavior is guaranteed; aborting browser work does not undo a server mutation or guarantee backend cancellation.

features.label: Typed links & parameters
features.definition: A route-aware API that checks destination names/paths and required route parameters before navigation. Generic language types, a string URL or runtime route matching alone do not qualify.

features.label: Validated URL state
features.definition: A router-owned or documented schema integration that parses and validates query/search parameters into typed application state, including malformed-input behavior. Raw URLSearchParams access alone does not qualify.

features.label: Navigation state retention
features.definition: A documented mechanism for retaining/restoring local UI or form state across navigation/back-forward. Identify persistent layouts, retained pages, DOM snapshots or serialization, and what resets. Browser caching alone is not a framework API.

features.label: Scroll restoration
features.definition: A router/navigation integration that restores scroll positions during history traversal. Identify window versus nested scrollports, opt-in configuration and reset controls. An imperative scrollTo helper alone does not qualify.

features.label: Unsaved-change guards
features.definition: An integrated navigation interception API that can pause/cancel an attempted route change and let the app resolve an unsaved-change prompt. Distinguish SPA navigation from browser beforeunload and its limitations.

features.label: Accessible navigation
features.definition: A documented soft-navigation integration for focus management or announcing route changes to assistive technology. Name which behavior is automatic and which remains application-owned. ARIA attributes alone do not qualify; native full-document navigation is distinguished.

features.label: Accessibility checks
features.definition: A documented compiler/linter/test integration that detects inaccessible authored UI. State static-analysis limits; no check establishes WCAG conformance, and emitting ARIA attributes alone does not qualify.

features.label: Deferred activation
features.definition: Activate an interactive SSR component/island through a documented visibility, idle, interaction or media trigger. Distinguish delaying activation from delaying the JavaScript download and describe any event replay. Lazy imports alone are not a hydration scheduler.

features.label: Route / island splitting
features.definition: An integrated build divides browser code by routes or independently activated islands so unused UI is not required in the initial bundle. Identify the splitting boundary and shared runtime; generic dynamic import syntax alone does not qualify.

features.label: Offline integration
features.definition: A documented service-worker/offline integration with build assets or cache lifecycle support. Applications must still define offline data/failure behavior; serving static files or a manifest alone is insufficient.

features.label: Scheduled tasks
features.definition: A documented recurring-task scheduler, distinct from merely dispatching or delaying one job. Describe the external runner, overlapping tasks and multi-server coordination rather than implying exactly-once execution.

features.label: Multi-channel notifications
features.definition: An application notification API that selects and formats multiple delivery channels. Email alone or low-level WebSocket messages do not qualify; provider credentials, queues and external channels are named separately.

features.label: Search indexing
features.definition: A documented application/model search integration with indexing and synchronization lifecycle, distinct from issuing a SQL LIKE query. Name engines/services and any application-owned synchronization.

features.label: Encrypted model fields
features.definition: A model/storage integration that transparently encrypts/decrypts configured attributes, with documented key management. A generic encryption function, password hashing or database disk encryption alone does not qualify.

features.label: HTTP integration tests
features.definition: A documented test harness for application handlers/routes with request construction and response assertions, including session/auth context where available. Unit renderer tests and browser automation are separate; state whether a network server is required.

official.label: Official package
official.description: Provided by a named first-party companion or adapter.

community.label: Third-party
community.description: Provided by a named external integration.

partial.label: Qualified
partial.description: A specific restriction, experimental API or application-owned recipe. Each cell names the qualification; this is not full support.

planned.label: Planned
planned.description: Explicitly listed on the reviewed roadmap.

unknown.label: Not reviewed
unknown.description: No support claim has been verified here. This does not mean unsupported.

undocumented.label: Not documented
undocumented.description: Reviewed the linked API or guide without establishing this behavior. This is not proof that an application cannot implement it.

scope.label: Outside scope
scope.description: Outside the reviewed core API; the host application or another framework can provide it.
